data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise sophisticated comparison structures including double comparatives, proportional comparison, superlative emphasis and similarity.
learningPoints: Use the + comparative..., the + comparative... for proportional relationships.
Use comparative and comparative to show gradual change.
Use by far, easily and one of the with superlatives.
Use no/not much/far + comparative to express degree.
Use nowhere near as...as for strong inequality.
Use comparison structures precisely in formal and informal contexts.

sections.explain: THE + comparative, THE + comparative expresses a linked change.

words.word: The more you practise, the more confident you become.
More you practise, more confident you become.
The more you practise, the most confident you become.

sections.summary: Using repeated comparatives for gradual change.
sections.explain: Comparative + AND + comparative expresses continuing change.

words.word: The situation is becoming more and more complicated.
The situation is becoming most and most complicated.
The situation is becoming more complicated and most complicated.

sections.explain: BY FAR strongly intensifies a superlative.

words.word: This is by far the best option.
This is by far better option.
This is the by far bestest option.

sections.summary: Using 'one of the + superlative + plural noun'.
sections.explain: After ONE OF THE + superlative, use a plural noun.

words.word: It is one of the most interesting books I've read.
It is one of the most interesting book I've read.
It is one of most interesting books I've read.

sections.explain: NOWHERE NEAR AS + adjective + AS expresses a large difference.

words.word: The second film was nowhere near as good as the first.
The second film was nowhere near so better than the first.
The second film was nowhere near as better as the first.

sections.explain: NOT MUCH + comparative indicates only a small difference.

words.word: This version isn't much cheaper than the old one.
This version isn't very cheapest than the old one.
This version isn't much more cheaper than the old one.
The new route is far more convenient.
The new route is far most convenient.
The new route is very more convenient.

sections.explain: EASILY can intensify a superlative meaning 'without doubt'.

words.word: She is easily the most experienced person on the team.
She is easily more experienced person on the team.
She is the easily most experience person on the team.

sections.explain: Use TWICE AS + adjective + AS to express a precise proportional comparison.

words.word: This room is twice as large as the other one.
This room is twice larger as the other one.
This room is two times more large than the other one.

sections.explain: Use THE SAME + noun + AS to compare equality of type or quality.

words.word: We bought the same model as you.
We bought the same model than you.
We bought same the model as you.
